formulations.label: Tablets
formulations.strengths: 5 mg (SmPC used; other strengths have their own SmPCs)

src.q: Each tablet contains 5 mg of amlodipine (as amlodipine besilate)

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: Hypertension; chronic stable angina; vasospastic (Prinzmetal's) angina.

src.q: Hypertension Chronic stable angina pectoris Vasospastic (Prinzmetal's) angina

restrictions.note: No prescribing restriction stated in the amlodipine 5 mg tablets SmPC.

items.t: Adults: start 5 mg once daily; may increase to a maximum of 10 mg once daily depending on response.

src.q: For both hypertension and angina the usual initial dose is 5 mg Amlodipine once daily which may be increased to a maximum dose of 10 mg depending on the individual patient's response.

items.t: Elderly: normal doses; increase the dose with care.

src.q: Normal dosage regimens are recommended in the elderly, but increase of the dosage should take place with care

items.t: No amlodipine dose adjustment is needed when given with thiazide diuretics, beta blockers or ACE inhibitors.

src.q: No dose adjustment of amlodipine is required upon concomitant administration of thiazide diuretics, beta blockers, and angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors.

items.t: Hypertension, 6 to 17 years: 2.5 mg once daily; increase to 5 mg once daily if blood pressure goal not reached after 4 weeks. Doses above 5 mg daily have not been studied in children.

src.q: The recommended antihypertensive oral dose in paediatric patients aged 6-17 years is 2.5 mg once daily as a starting dose, up-titrated to 5 mg once daily if blood pressure goal is not achieved after 4 weeks.
Doses in excess of 5 mg daily have not been studied in paediatric patients

items.t: Under 6 years: no data available.

src.q: Children under 6 years old No data are available.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to amlodipine, other dihydropyridines or any excipient.

src.q: hypersensitivity to the active substance, dihydropyridine derivatives or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1

items.t: Severe hypotension; shock (including cardiogenic shock).

src.q: severe hypotension shock (including cardiogenic shock)

items.t: Left ventricular outflow tract obstruction (e.g. high-grade aortic stenosis).

src.q: obstruction of the outflow tract of the left ventricle (e.g. high-grade aortic stenosis)

items.t: Haemodynamically unstable heart failure after acute myocardial infarction.

src.q: haemodynamically unstable heart failure after acute myocardial infarction

items.t: Heart failure: use with caution. In severe heart failure (NYHA III-IV) more pulmonary oedema was reported with amlodipine than placebo; calcium-channel blockers may increase the risk of future cardiovascular events and mortality in congestive heart failure.

src.q: Patients with heart failure should be treated with caution.
Calcium channel blockers, including amlodipine, should be used with caution in patients with congestive heart failure, as they may increase the risk of future cardiovascular events and mortality.

items.t: Hepatic impairment: half-life prolonged and exposure higher; start at the lower end of the dose range and use caution when starting and when increasing the dose.

src.q: Amlodipine should therefore be initiated at the lower end of the dosing range and caution should be used, both on initial treatment and when increasing the dose.

items.t: Safety and efficacy in hypertensive crisis not established.

src.q: The safety and efficacy of amlodipine in hypertensive crisis has not been established.

items.t: Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. clarithromycin, erythromycin, azole antifungals, protease inhibitors, diltiazem, verapamil): amlodipine exposure may rise markedly, with more risk of hypotension (more so in the elderly). Clinical monitoring and dose adjustment may be needed.

src.q: Concomitant use of amlodipine with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors (protease inhibitors, azole antifungals, macrolides like erythromycin or clarithromycin, verapamil or diltiazem) may give rise to significant increase in amlodipine exposure
Clinical monitoring and dose adjustment may thus be required.

items.t: CYP3A4 inducers (e.g. rifampicin, St John's wort): amlodipine levels may change. Monitor blood pressure and consider dose adjustment during and after the combination.

src.q: blood pressure should be monitored and dose regulation considered both during and after concomitant medication particularly with strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g. rifampicin, hypericum perforatum).

items.t: Simvastatin: limit simvastatin to 20 mg daily in patients taking amlodipine (amlodipine 10 mg raised simvastatin exposure by 77%). MHRA: the 20 mg maximum applies with amlodipine 5 mg and 10 mg.

src.q: Limit the dose of simvastatin in patients on amlodipine to 20 mg daily.
The maximum recommended dose of simvastatin co-administered with amlodipine or diltiazem is now 20 mg per day.
the recommendation for a maximum daily dose of simvastatin of 20 mg applies with amlodipine at doses of both 10 mg and 5 mg.

items.t: Other antihypertensives: additive blood pressure lowering.

src.q: The blood pressure lowering effects of amlodipine adds to the blood pressure-lowering effects of other medicinal products with antihypertensive properties.

items.t: Grapefruit or grapefruit juice: not recommended (may increase blood pressure lowering).

src.q: Administration of amlodipine with grapefruit or grapefruit juice is not recommended

items.t: Tacrolimus: risk of raised tacrolimus levels; monitor tacrolimus levels and adjust its dose. Ciclosporin (renal transplant): consider monitoring ciclosporin levels and reducing its dose as needed.

src.q: administration of amlodipine in a patient treated with tacrolimus requires monitoring of tacrolimus blood levels and dose adjustment of tacrolimus when appropriate.
Consideration should be given for monitoring ciclosporin levels in renal transplant patients on amlodipine

items.t: Atorvastatin, digoxin and warfarin: amlodipine did not affect their pharmacokinetics in interaction studies.

src.q: amlodipine did not affect the pharmacokinetics of atorvastatin, digoxin or warfarin

items.t: Dantrolene infusion / malignant hyperthermia: avoid calcium-channel blockers such as amlodipine in patients susceptible to malignant hyperthermia and in its management (risk of hyperkalaemia; ventricular fibrillation and collapse seen in animals with verapamil plus IV dantrolene).

src.q: it is recommended that the co-administration of calcium channel blockers such as amlodipine be avoided in patients susceptible to malignant hyperthermia and in the management of malignant hyperthermia
In animals, lethal ventricular fibrillation and cardiovascular collapse are observed in association with hyperkalaemia after administration of verapamil and intravenous dantrolene.

items.t: mTOR inhibitors (sirolimus, temsirolimus, everolimus): amlodipine is a weak CYP3A inhibitor and may increase their exposure.

src.q: mTOR inhibitors such as sirolimus, temsirolimus, and everolimus are CYP3A substrates.
With concomitant use of mTOR inhibitors, amlodipine may increase exposure of mTOR inhibitors.

items.t: Normal dose in renal impairment (plasma levels do not correlate with degree of renal impairment). Not dialysable.

src.q: Changes in amlodipine plasma concentrations are not correlated with degree of renal impairment, therefore the normal dosage is recommended.
Amlodipine is not dialysable.

items.t: Mild to moderate hepatic impairment: no established dose; choose the dose cautiously and start at the lower end of the range.

src.q: Dosage recommendations have not been established in patients with mild to moderate hepatic impairment, therefore dose selection should be cautious and should start at the lower end of the dosing range

items.t: Severe hepatic impairment: not studied; start at the lowest dose and titrate slowly. Careful monitoring may be needed.

src.q: Amlodipine should be initiated at the lowest dose and titrated slowly in patients with severe hepatic impairment.
Slow dose titration and careful monitoring may be required in patients with severe hepatic impairment.

items.t: SmPC: safety in human pregnancy not established. Use only when there is no safer alternative and the disease itself carries greater risk for mother and fetus.

src.q: The safety of amlodipine in human pregnancy has not been established.
Use in pregnancy is only recommended when there is no safer alternative and when the disease itself carries greater risk for the mother and foetus.

items.t: BUMPS (calcium-channel blockers leaflet): no clear risks from calcium-channel blockers in pregnancy; nifedipine is the one commonly used. Others are less used and recommended only when benefit outweighs possible risk. No extra monitoring for major birth defects is needed.

src.q: There are no clear risks of taking a calcium channel blocker in pregnancy.

The other calcium channel blockers are less commonly used, and while not thought to cause problems, will only be recommended if the benefits of treating a potentially serious or lifestyle-impacting condition outweigh any possible risks.
No extra monitoring for major birth defects is required following use of a calcium channel blocker.

items.t: SmPC: amlodipine passes into breast milk (infant dose estimated at 3-7% of maternal dose, maximum 15%). Weigh the benefit of breastfeeding against the benefit of treatment.

src.q: Amlodipine is excreted in human milk.

A decision on whether to continue/discontinue breast-feeding or to continue/discontinue therapy with amlodipine should be made taking into account the benefit of breast-feeding to the child and the benefit of amlodipine therapy to the mother.

items.t: SPS: use with caution; nifedipine is the preferred dihydropyridine. As a precaution, watch the infant for hypotension (drowsiness, lethargy, pallor, poor feeding, poor weight gain). Advice applies to full-term, healthy infants.

src.q: It can be used with caution during breastfeeding, but nifedipine is the preferred dihydropyridine calcium-channel blocker.
As a precaution, monitor the infant for hypotension which may manifest as drowsiness, lethargy, looking pale , poor feeding and inadequate weight gain.
Recommendations apply to full term and healthy infants only.

items.t: Reversible changes in the head of spermatozoa have been reported with calcium-channel blockers; clinical data on fertility are insufficient.

src.q: Reversible biochemical changes in the head of spermatozoa have been reported in some patients treated by calcium channel blockers.
Clinical data are insufficient regarding the potential effect of amlodipine on fertility.

items.t: Very common: oedema. Common: somnolence, dizziness, headache, palpitations, flushing, abdominal pain, nausea, dyspepsia, altered bowel habit, ankle swelling, muscle cramps, visual disturbance, dyspnoea, fatigue, asthenia.

src.q: The most commonly reported adverse reactions during treatment are somnolence, dizziness, headache, palpitations, flushing, abdominal pain, nausea, ankle swelling, oedema and fatigue.
General disorders and administration site conditions Very common Oedema Common Fatigue, asthenia

items.t: Very rare: angioedema, erythema multiforme, exfoliative dermatitis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome; toxic epidermal necrolysis (frequency not known).

src.q: Very rare Angioedema, erythema multiforme, exfoliative dermatitis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, Quincke oedema, photosensitivity Not known Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis

items.t: Very rare: hepatitis, jaundice, raised liver enzymes (mostly cholestatic); pancreatitis; leucopenia, thrombocytopenia; myocardial infarction.

src.q: Very rare Hepatitis, jaundice, hepatic enzymes increased*
Very rare Pancreatitis, gastritis, gingival hyperplasia
Very rare Leukocytopenia, thrombocytopenia
Very rare Myocardial infarction

items.t: Overdose: marked, possibly prolonged hypotension up to fatal shock; non-cardiogenic pulmonary oedema may appear 24-48 hours after ingestion. Dialysis unlikely to help.

src.q: Marked and probably prolonged systemic hypotension up to and including shock with fatal outcome have been reported.
Non-cardiogenic pulmonary oedema has rarely been reported as a consequence of amlodipine overdose that may manifest with a delayed onset (24-48 hours post-ingestion) and require ventilatory support.

items.t: With CYP3A4 inducers: monitor blood pressure during and after the combination.

src.q: blood pressure should be monitored and dose regulation considered both during and after concomitant medication

items.t: Severe hepatic impairment: slow titration and careful monitoring may be needed.

src.q: Slow dose titration and careful monitoring may be required in patients with severe hepatic impairment.

items.t: With tacrolimus: monitor tacrolimus blood levels.

src.q: requires monitoring of tacrolimus blood levels

items.t: Oral, once daily. Food does not affect absorption.

src.q: The bioavailability of amlodipine is not affected by food intake.

items.t: Dizziness, headache, tiredness or nausea can affect driving; take care especially at the start of treatment.

src.q: If patients taking amlodipine suffer from dizziness, headache, fatigue or nausea the ability to react may be impaired.
Caution is recommended especially at the start of treatment.

items.t: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice.

src.q: Administration of amlodipine with grapefruit or grapefruit juice is not recommended

items.t: Ankle swelling and oedema are common.

src.q: Musculoskeletal and connective tissue disorders Common Ankle swelling, muscle cramps
